accepted.sentence: On a descent, riders often keep the pedals level so neither pedal catches the ground while cornering.
On bumpy trails, flexed elbows and knees absorb impacts and help keep the tires in contact with the surface.
During a short, steep climb, a rider may stand on the pedals to apply force through each stroke.
In a group, riders leave enough space ahead to react safely if the person in front slows suddenly.
Before turning in traffic, a rider can extend an arm to communicate the intended direction to nearby road users.
Cargo is more stable when secured low and centered, reducing the effect of shifting weight on steering.
After riding through rain, drying exposed metal parts and lubricating the chain helps limit corrosion and wear.
When walking through a crowded area, a rider dismounts and guides the frame by its handlebars.
